 Early voting opens across New York State Saturday 
 Early voting kicked off Saturday and some wasted no time in casting their ballot. By Seth Appleby and 7 News Staff Published : Oct. 24, 2026 at 6:06 PM EDT | Updated : 1 hour ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google WATERTOWN, New York (WWNY) - Early voting kicked off Saturday and some wasted no time in casting their ballot.
 “Always been passionate in being involved in government and having our say,” said Meghan Hernandez. “Especially this midterms, I feel like there’s a lot riding and we just wanted to put our voices out there early and get it done.”
 Early voting and absentee voting by mail has become a popular choice among people. Poll workers at the Jefferson County Office Building location say within the first two hours, they’ve had nearly 200 people cast a ballot.
 “Nursing, police officers, military. It’s just so convenient for them to get out on the weekend or in the evening to be able to vote,” said Tiffany Ladd, Republican Commissioner at the Jefferson County Board of Elections. “It’s absolutely wonderful.”
 “To have it up to a few weeks versus one day opens that opportunity to so many more people,” said Hernandez. “You also never know, you might think you can get out that day and then something might happen, so to have that extra time to get out just helps so many people.”
 Some people like the convenience of voting at any time. Others, like Paul Dodge, are looking to avoid the long lines of Election Day.
 “I don’t know if any of the locations would have changed or how long the lines would be on voting day in November,” said Dodge.
 Jefferson County Board of Election officials say so far they’ve issued over 2,700 absentee ballots and have received nearly 1,500 back. Early Voting runs until November 1st, Election Day is Tuesday November 3rd.
 Jefferson County locations and hours
 In Jefferson County, those looking to cast their ballot early can do so at the County Office Building in downtown Watertown or at the Depauville Fire Hall, which is fairly new. Officials say that location has become a convenient option for those north of Watertown.
 In Jefferson County, voters can cast ballots at either location from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Hours will switch to noon to 8 p.m. on Oct. 26 and Oct. 28.
 Lewis County locations and hours
 Lewis County voters can cast their ballots at the Board of Elections building in Lowville from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Those hours will switch to noon to 8 p.m. on Oct. 27 and Oct. 29.
 St. Lawrence County locations and hours
 In St. Lawrence County, voters can cast ballots early at the Potsdam Central School Annex or the Dobisky Center in Ogdensburg. Hours are 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily.
